title: ContainRE run policy (v1)
description: Declarative, per-run policy. Drives reproducible headless/API launches, and the effective policy is persisted into the run directory. Additive-only within major version 1.

specimen.description: What to run and how it is invoked.

path.description: Path (host-side) to the ELF specimen to analyze.

container_path.description: Optional Docker-only path used to execute the specimen inside the container. Defaults to /specimen.

stdin.description: Path to a file fed as the specimen's stdin, or null.

env.description: Environment variables presented to the specimen.

limits.description: Per-run resource ceilings, enforced via cgroups and a wall-clock timer.

network.description: Network posture. Default uses a simulated-internet sink with no real egress; real egress requires posture=allow or an explicit allowlist entry.

posture.description: deny = no responders (attempts fail, still traced); simulate = built-in loopback sink answers supported protocols; allow = real egress (dangerous).

simulate.description: Bring up the built-in NetSink responder. Implied by posture=simulate.

mitm.description: Transparent TLS interception with an injected CA (detectable; off by default).

docker_network.description: DockerRuntime network attachment. auto preserves ContainRE defaults; bridge attaches Docker bridge when real egress is explicitly allowed; host uses host networking and is accepted only with a non-empty ptrace allowlist; none forces --network none.

allow.description: Allowlist of real egress targets as host:port or ip:port (port optional = any).

sink.description: Built-in simulated-internet responder configuration. h2-grpc-replay is experimental and answers configured gRPC methods without contacting the real service.

unary_methods.description: Method-name substrings to treat as unary gRPC calls. Matching is byte-substring based on HTTP/2 header blocks.

streaming_methods.description: Method-name substrings to treat as streaming gRPC calls. Matching is byte-substring based on HTTP/2 header blocks.

unary_response_hex.description: Uncompressed protobuf response body for unary calls, encoded as hex. Empty string sends an empty protobuf message.

stream_initial_response_hex.description: Uncompressed protobuf response body for the first message on a configured streaming call.

stream_response_hex.description: Uncompressed protobuf response body for later messages on a configured streaming call.

record_payloads.description: Record bounded previews of inbound gRPC DATA payloads in sink interaction events. Useful for protocol diagnosis; keep false for minimal evidence.

payload_preview_bytes.description: Maximum bytes retained per recorded gRPC payload preview.

payload_record_limit.description: Maximum number of gRPC payload preview records retained per sink interaction.

negative_feature_substrings.description: Request payload byte-substrings that should receive a configured gRPC error instead of a normal replay response. This is useful when a real service rejects feature probes.

negative_grpc_status.description: gRPC status code to send for negative_feature_substrings matches.

negative_grpc_message.description: gRPC message template for negative_feature_substrings matches. The literal {feature} is replaced with the matched substring.
negative_grpc_message.default: feature {feature} is not expected to exist in the server

listen_port.description: Optional fixed loopback port for the built-in sink. Use this with trace.tracer=none and hostname-to-loopback mapping when no ptrace redirection is available.

extra_hosts.description: Docker-only host-to-IP entries added to /etc/hosts with --add-host for controlled analyses that need deterministic name resolution without opening DNS.

work_mount.description: Host directory mounted read-write at cwd; sample files dropped here.

read_only_mounts.description: Additional host paths mounted read-only by DockerRuntime for dependency trees, config bundles, or fixtures. LocalRuntime ignores this because it already runs on the host filesystem.

decoys.description: Canary files (relative to work_mount) planted to trip ransomware/stealer behavior; access is a high-signal event.

tracer.description: ptrace records syscall-level behavior and redirects simulated egress. none launches the specimen directly for low-overhead benchmarks; combine with Docker --network none, hostname-to-loopback mapping, and a fixed sink listen_port.

l1.description: Always-on L1 syscall/event classes to record.

snapshot_on.description: Triggers that capture a memory snapshot. The gate value is reserved for future live-decision events and accepted for forward compatibility; the current tracer emits the other triggers.

snapshot_every_ms.description: Periodic snapshot interval in ms; 0 = triggers only.

window.description: Bound for L2 tracing. Exactly one bound kind is expected when mode != off.

time_ms.description: Trace for this many ms of specimen time.

until_io.description: Trace until the next I/O syscall.

detect.description: Behavioral detection toggles (run over raw facts).

attack_tags.description: Map findings to MITRE ATT&CK technique ids.

yara_rules.description: Paths to additional YARA rule files/dirs.

instrumentation.description: Opt-in invasive runtime instrumentation. These features can perturb target behavior and must be called out in evidence.

tls_plaintext.description: OpenSSL LD_PRELOAD instrumentation for TLS plaintext observation or experimental response replay. Replay mode fakes OpenSSL handshake/write/read behavior and is weaker evidence than protocol-faithful network emulation.

provider.description: Instrumentation provider. openssl-preload hooks OpenSSL symbols with LD_PRELOAD.

mode.description: observe records SSL_read/SSL_write plaintext while preserving real TLS calls. replay is experimental and returns synthetic SSL_read data while faking OpenSSL handshake/write success.

output.description: Path, as seen by the specimen, for JSONL plaintext capture output. Defaults to tls_plaintext_capture.log in the work directory.

replay_file.description: Host-side transcript file for replay mode. Lines may be hex strings or JSONL records with direction=in and a hex field.

fake_handshake.description: Experimental replay fallback. When true, the shim fakes OpenSSL handshake success instead of using a real local TLS/MITM handshake. This is highly invasive and lower-fidelity.

libssl.description: Optional in-process path to an already-loaded private libssl.so.3 used when RTLD_NEXT cannot resolve OpenSSL symbols.

runtime.description: Runtime-side helper commands executed inside the same namespace as the specimen. Use these for local services required by a batch run; setup commands run before the specimen, teardown commands run afterward.

setup_commands.description: Shell commands run before the specimen starts. A non-zero exit code aborts the specimen run.

teardown_commands.description: Shell commands run after the specimen exits or setup fails. Non-zero exit codes are logged but do not replace the specimen exit code.

command_shell.description: Absolute shell path used for setup and teardown commands.

command_timeout_s.description: Per-command timeout in seconds for setup and teardown commands.

docker_reuse_container.description: DockerRuntime-only no-trace mode. When true, execute this run in a long-lived matching container with docker exec instead of starting a fresh docker run.

docker_reuse_key.description: Stable key for the reusable Docker container. Policies with incompatible mounts or network settings recreate the keyed container.

docker_user.description: DockerRuntime-only user passed to docker run/exec via --user, for example '1000:1000'. Null or empty means Docker's image default user.

report.description: Post-hoc reporting and evidence assertions. Assertions are evaluated by summarize/reporting commands after the run; they never alter specimen execution.

assertions.description: Reusable evidence checks evaluated against summary metrics such as network.remote_endpoint_event_count, artifacts.names, or exit_code.

value.description: Expected value. Type depends on op; match ops accept one pattern or a list of patterns.

match.description: Pattern mode for any_match, none_match, and all_match.

severity.description: Severity assigned if the assertion fails.
